messages.subject: INLA deterministic?
parts:
While playing around with different prior precisions for the fixed effects in a model, it appears that INLA produces very different results when a model is refitted several times (both in terms of DIC and e.g. posterior means, see below).  I was under the impression that INLA is a completely deterministic algorithm so I'm very surprised by this.  I suppose I have overlooked something here?  Results become identical if using the default prior precision of 0.001.

> a1 <- inla(y2 ~ tfactor + f(femid,model="iid") + z + z2 + f(tfactor,z,model="rw1"),
+            "zeroinflatedpoisson1",
+            control.fixed=list(mean=0,prec=0.000001),
+            control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
+            data=hvdata)
> a2 <- inla(y2 ~ tfactor + f(femid,model="iid") + z + z2 + f(tfactor,z,model="rw1"),
+            "zeroinflatedpoisson1",
+            control.fixed=list(mean=0,prec=0.000001),
+            control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),
+            data=hvdata)
> a1$dic$dic
[1] 16373.27
> a2$dic$dic
[1] 16364.97
> ((a2$summary.fixed-a1$summary.fixed)/a1$summary.fixed)[,1]

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA deterministic?
parts:
Ok, thanks. This seems related to the inclusion of the iid random effect based on female identity (femid) which according to 

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-INLA-seems-to-work-great-for-near-all-cases-but-are-there-cases-where-INLA-is-known-to-have-problems-

could be problematic given that many females (1544 out of 2220 in our data) are only observed once?  At least the problem disappears if removing the iid femid term.  This is somewhat unsatisfactory, however, since we want to account for the dependency between observations for females observed multiple times.

I also tried the control.inla=list(correct=TRUE,correct.factor=10) in the testing version but dic values are still vastly different for the same model refitted several times...

J

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA deterministic?
parts:
On Wed, 2015-05-20 at 03:45 -0700, Jarle Tufto wrote:
> I was under the impression that INLA is a completely deterministic
> algorithm so I'm very surprised by this. I suppose I have overlooked
> something here? Results become

to answer this formally; the method itself is completely deterministic,
but the implementation is strictly speaking, not. the parallellism is
beyond our control by design (openMP), which might be a small issue if
the optimizer does not converge completely. you might see differences in
the n'th digit, say. setting control.inla=list(tolerance=1e-6), say
usually improces this. (default 0.005)

adding or adding not, a random effect, can have a big impact, I have
seen before, which is usually a model/data issue.

H


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
